    Power for prediction-powered linear regression (OLS) estimator

    power_ppi_ols.Rd

    Computes the analytical (normal-theory) power for a two-sided Wald test on a linear contrast \(c^\top \beta\) in the prediction-powered linear regression (PPI-OLS) framework.

    power_ppi_ols(delta, V_u, V_l, N, n, c, alpha = 0.05)

    Arguments

    delta

    Numeric scalar. True effect size for the linear contrast \(c^\top (\beta - \beta_0)\).

    V_u

    Numeric \(p \times p\) matrix. Sandwich variance for the unlabeled (imputed) OLS term.

    V_l

    Numeric \(p \times p\) matrix. Sandwich variance for the labeled (rectifier) OLS term.

    N

    Integer. Unlabeled sample size.

    n

    Integer. Labeled sample size.

    c

    Numeric vector of length \(p\). Linear contrast to test; e.g. to test coefficient \(j\), set c = e_j.

    alpha

    Numeric scalar in (0, 1). Two-sided significance level.

    Value

    Numeric scalar: the analytical (normal-theory) power \(1-\beta\) of the two-sided test.

    Examples

    # Example: 2D regression with modest effect
set.seed(1)
p <- 2
V_u <- matrix(c(1.0, 0.2, 0.2, 0.8), ncol = p)
V_l <- matrix(c(0.9, 0.1, 0.1, 0.7), ncol = p)
N <- 2000
n <- 200
c <- c(1, 0)     # test first coefficient
delta <- 0.15

power_ppi_ols(delta, V_u, V_l, N, n, c, alpha = 0.05)
#> [1] 0.564116

# Test second coefficient (different direction)
c2 <- c(0, 1)
power_ppi_ols(delta = 0.10, V_u, V_l, N, n, c2)
#> [1] 0.3601009
